title: Age-Related Functional Shift of Chronic Low Back Pain and the Role of Sagittal Spinopelvic Alignment During Gait: A Comparative Analysis of Middle-Aged and Oldest-Old Patient Populations
content: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to elucidate the age-related functional transformation of chronic low back pain (LBP) across distinct dynamic conditions and to investigate its relationship with standing sagittal spinopelvic alignment in middle-aged and oldest-old cohorts. Methods: This cross-sectional, retrospective study evaluated 102 patients with chronic LBP, categorized into Group M (under 75 years; n = 51) and Group O (75 years or older; n = 51). Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores and proportional pain contributions (VAS%) were assessed during rest, getting up, rolling over, and walking (gait). Standing radiographic spinopelvic parameters—including lumbar lordosis (LL), pelvic tilt (PT), and pelvic incidence–lumbar lordosis mismatch (PI–LL)—were correlated with these pain profiles. Results: Group M reported significantly higher absolute pain intensity during rest, getting up, and rolling over (p<0.001). Conversely, absolute gait pain intensity did not differ between groups (p=0.730), whereas the proportional contribution of walking pain (Gait VAS%) was markedly higher in Group O (p < 0.001). Radiographically, Group O exhibited a severe loss of LL (p = 0.001) and a greater PI–LL mismatch (p = 0.003). Multiple regression analysis confirmed that a greater standing PI–LL mismatch independently and significantly predicted an elevated proportional walking pain profile (β = 0.27). Conclusions: Chronic LBP undergoes a distinct age-related functional shift. While middle-aged patients experience higher absolute pain intensity in non-weight-bearing states, symptoms in oldest-old patients concentrate heavily during active ambulation. This functional shift is independently driven by standing sagittal alignment mismatches, highlighting the clinical necessity of dynamic, weight-bearing evaluations for precise geriatric LBP management.
